title: conntrack exhaustion: eBPF/iptables mismatch wip
content:
Summary:

This is a working incident note for the partial outage on 2025-11-03 where a subset of nodes experienced pod-to-pod packet loss and high system CPU on kubelet/cni processes. Symptoms looked like scheduling delays, liveness probe failures, and intermittent Kubernetes API errors from kube-proxy timeouts. The immediate mitigation was to cordon and drain the most affected nodes and roll a cni daemonset update with a config that disables an eBPF fastpath that appears to have been interacting badly with iptables/nft rules on our kernel version.

Impact:
- ~12% of nodes in cluster-us-west-2-a showed >15% packet loss and elevated conntrack table utilization.
- Several stateful pods (datastores, model-servers) reported connection resets; autoscaler saw flapping and briefly evicted jobs.
- Customer-facing latency spikes for model inference requests for 18 minutes in the 11:12-11:30 window.

Detection and Alerts:
- Alert: "conntrack_high_utilization" (threshold: 85% open entries) fired at 2025-11-03T11:06:22Z for nodes: node-0142, node-0145, node-0150.
- Synthetic health-check ping failed to 3 pods at 11:09.
- On-call grabbed PagerDuty, jumped into #incident-sre Slack channel.

Timeline (UTC):
- 11:04 - Gradual increase in conntrack usage observed in dashboards (10%->70% over 6 minutes).
- 11:06 - conntrack_high_utilization alert fires for three nodes.
- 11:07 - First on-call message; begin rolling checks (ss, netstat, conntrack -L counts).
- 11:09 - API server logs show high request latency and 504s for certain endpoints.
- 11:12 - Cordon & drain recommended for node-0145 and node-0150; traffic shifted.
- 11:15 - Temporary cni-daemonset rollout that disables eBPF offload applied (config flag: ENABLE_EBPF=false).
- 11:22 - Conntrack usage starts dropping; packet loss reports reduced.
- 11:30 - Incident declared mitigated. Post-incident monitoring continued for 2 hours.

Checks performed (quick commands executed during triage):
- Check conntrack counts: sudo conntrack -C && sudo conntrack -S
- Inspect kernel conntrack table: sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
- Check dmesg for XDP/eBPF errors: sudo dmesg | grep -i ebpf
- Check nftables/iptables incompat warnings: sudo iptables -L -n -v; sudo nft list ruleset | head -n 50
- See kube-proxy mode and CNI: kubectl -n kube-system get ds cni -o yaml | grep -i mode

Preliminary root cause analysis (hypothesis):
- The observed pattern points at a mismatch between eBPF programs installed by our CNI (v0.9.1) and the kernel's nftables/iptables translation layer on nodes running kernel 6.2.x. When both nftables and legacy iptables rules existed (we still had iptables-legacy present in the image), some packets bypassed expected conntrack lifecycle paths leading to stale conntrack entries and unnatural growth.
- eBPF was used to implement fast-path NAT/hairpinning optimizations. Under high service churn these eBPF maps produced flows that did not decrement conntrack entries in the kernel as expected, or the garbage collection cadence between the eBPF map and kernel conntrack was mismatched.
- Additionally, kube-proxy was running in iptables mode on these nodes while others were in IPVS mode; differences in connection tracking semantics between IPVS and iptables likely amplified the issue.

Evidence supporting hypothesis:
- dmesg on affected nodes shows repeated WARNs from cni-ebpf: "map_lookup failed: no entry" and occasional "nf_conntrack: table full" kernel logs.
- Nodes with iptables-nft (compat layer) but also iptables-legacy installed saw higher counts.
- When we disabled eBPF fastpath in the CNI daemonset, conntrack growth rate dropped within a minute.

Immediate Mitigations applied:
1) Cordon + drain the most affected nodes to stop churn forcing new connections onto them.
2) Redeploy CNI daemonset with ENABLE_EBPF=false to disable the fastpath.
3) Increase conntrack table size on hot nodes temporarily as stopgap: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=131072
4) Restart kube-proxy on affected nodes (after draining) to ensure clean rule install.

Runbook draft (actions to standardize):
- Trigger conditions:
  - Alert: conntrack_high_utilization AND packet loss > 5% in last 5m
  - Service probe failures for >=3 pods in 5m
- Triage checklist:
  - Identify nodes with high conntrack usage (metric: nf_conntrack_count).
  - Run: sudo conntrack -L | wc -l and sudo conntrack -S.
  - Check kernel messages: sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i -E "conntrack|ebpf|nf_conntrack|nft|iptables"
  - Determine kube-proxy mode: kubectl get ds -n kube-system kube-proxy -o yaml | grep mode
  - Check CNI version: kubectl -n kube-system get ds cni -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
  - If eBPF-related errors are present, consider disabling eBPF on the daemonset and rolling out to a small percentage first.
- Mitigation steps (ordered):
  1) If node CPU > 60% and conntrack > 90%: cordon & drain node.
  2) If multiple nodes impacted: roll CNI config (disable eBPF) with canary rollout (5% of nodes) and monitor.
  3) If immediate pressure persists: increase nf_conntrack_max as temporary relief and restart kube-proxy.
  4) Do not reboot nodes unless kernel logs explicitly recommend it.

Permanent fixes and follow-ups (owners assigned):
- SRE/Networking (Marcus Lee) to test CNI v0.10 in staging across kernel versions 5.15->6.5 to reproduce and root-cause eBPF/conntrack lifecycle mismatch. Target: 2025-11-17.
- Platform Eng (Elena Park) to add node image validation step in our CI that checks iptables/nft alternatives and ensures iptables-nft-only configuration prior to rollout. Target: 2025-11-12.
- Runtime team to update deployment policy to prefer kube-proxy IPVS mode for high-throughput clusters; document the decision and rollout plan (Diego Ruiz). Target: 2025-11-24.
- Observability (Aisha Gupta) to add a dedicated dashboard: "conntrack lifecycle" with 1m and 5m growth rates, per-node dmesg error surfacing, and correlate with eBPF map usage. Target: 2025-11-10 (initial).

Monitoring & alerts changes proposed:
- Add an alert for "conntrack_growth_rate" when net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count increases >500 entries in 1m.
- Flag when dmesg contains eBPF or nf_conntrack WARN/ERR strings and route to SRE.
- Signal to create a synthetic probe per node that validates basic pod-to-pod TCP connectivity across the service mesh to catch hairpin/NAT issues sooner.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did only certain kernel versions show the failure under our workload? Is this a known kernel regression with the nftables compatibility layer?
- Do we have any user workloads that program raw iptables rules that conflict with CNI-managed rules? Need inventory.
- Could IPVS mode have prevented or worsened this? We saw mixed behavior across clusters. Need a controlled test matrix.

Postmortem next steps (this doc is a working draft):
- Run controlled chaos test in staging to intentionally create service churn and replicate conntrack growth with eBPF enabled (owner Marcus).
- Validate a stable configuration: cni v0.10 + iptables-nft-only + kernel 6.1.x in staging before promoting to production.
- Finalize runbook and publish to: https://console.redwood.com/runbooks/conntrack (placeholder).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider building a light-weight agent that watches for eBPF map entries older than X and correlates them to conntrack entries (might help debugging).
- Add a gating test to our node image build to prevent packaging iptables-legacy.

References and quick links:
- Jira: SRE-482 (investigation)
- GitHub: redwood-inference/k8s-cni#78 (CNI eBPF map bug)
- Slack thread: #incident-sre (2025-11-03)

If you worked on triage, add notes below and call out anything I missed. This will become the postmortem skeleton once owners confirm repro steps.
